title: structured-output: add grammar and regex constrained-decoding backends and tokenizer edge-case fixes
author: Maya Patel
merge_outcome: merged — automated canary rollout to 10% then full
description: Motivation: users rely on structured output guarantees for tool/function calling and downstream parsers. Existing constrained decoding supported only a single DFA-style backend and had gaps around grammar (CFG) handling, complex regex constraints and tokenizer boundary edge cases which caused malformed JSON outputs and streaming truncation for long tokens. This PR introduces two new constrained-decoding backends (CFG-based and regex-based) plus a lightweight middleware that normalizes tokenization boundaries to prevent split-token constraint violations. The change is backwards-compatible with the existing DFA backend and the OpenAI-compat API surface; new backends are selectable via the existing constrained_decoding configuration (backend: dfa|cfg|regex). Implementation notes: 1) Added a CFG backend that compiles a user-provided context-free grammar into a compact LR-like table and performs incremental parse-state tracking during streaming decoding. 2) Added a regex-backend that compiles anchored regular expressions into NFAs and uses a bounded lookahead to validate incremental token sequences. 3) Introduced a tokenizer-normalizer that maps partial tokens to canonical boundary-aware units to avoid matches being split across streaming chunks. 4) Updated the OpenAI-compat layer to accept the new backend parameter and to expose detailed failure reasons (e.g., "regex_no_progress", "cfg_unexpected_token"). Performance: CFG and regex paths are optimized for common cases; DFA remains the fastest for simple prefix constraints. Safety: all user-supplied grammars/regexes are compiled in a sandboxed interpreter with strict resource limits to prevent ReDoS or explosion in compile time. Testing: extensive unit tests and property tests added, alongside a new end-to-end streaming test that replays problematic prompts from customer incidents. Rollout: feature is behind a feature-flag and will be rolled out to canary tenants for two weeks before enabling by default. See release_notes for compatibility and migration steps.

release_notes: Added CFG and regex constrained-decoding backends; selectable via constrained_decoding.backend (dfa|cfg|regex)
Tokenizer-normalizer prevents split-token constraint violations in streaming responses
OpenAI-compat: new error codes exposed for debugging constrained-decoding failures
Default remains backward compatible; feature behind feature-flag for canary rollout
migration_steps: If you used custom DFAs, no action required. To opt into CFG/regex behavior set constrained_decoding.backend in your call params or account config.
Large or untrusted grammars should be audited; the sandbox enforces a 500ms compile limit and memory caps.
If you rely on deterministic lowest-latency path, continue using dfa backend—CFG/regex may be slower for simple prefixes.
